title: Your own exceptions
kind: a core chapter: every rule in the register form, the log in and the games uses what you make here
one: You make your own exceptions, one for each way a player can break a rule. Then the Player class checks every rule as each value is set, and throws the right exception.

stages.title: See the rules, and what an exception is

screens.title: See what this chapter makes, and the words it uses

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know what an exception is, and why Summit Ready has its own exceptions.
At the moment, Player takes any username at all, even a blank one. This chapter gives Player its rules, so a bad username or password is refused at once.
When a rule is broken, the code throws an exception. The exception stops the code, and carries a message that tells the player what to fix.

need: About 2 hours. Your ticks are kept, so you can stop at the end of any screen and come back later.

words: char.IsDigit
Says whether one letter of some text is a digit, from 0 to 9.
Contains
`value.Contains("|")` is true when the bar is anywhere in the text.
try and catch
Code inside `try` runs. If it throws an exception, the matching `catch` runs, and the program does not crash.
exception
A message the code sends out when something has gone wrong. It stops the code until a `catch` deals with it.
throw
`throw` stops the method at once, and hands an exception to whatever code called it.
inherit
A class that inherits from another class gets everything the other class has. `: SummitException` after a class name means it inherits from SummitException.
base
`: base(message)` hands the message to the class it inherits from, which keeps it.
try
A `try` block holds code that might throw an exception.
catch
A `catch` block runs when code in the `try` block throws an exception.
Message
The words an exception carries, such as **Type a username.**
Trim
Takes the spaces off the start and the end of some words.
Length
How many characters some words have.
char
One character, such as a letter, a digit or a space.
rule
Something a player must do, such as type a username of 3 to 12 characters. Each rule is checked in the code.
blocks.intro: You do not need to learn these words now. Where you first meet each one in the chapter, it has a dotted line under it. Hover over it or tap it to see what it means.

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know the 11 rules a new player must follow, and which class checks each one.
Each [[rule|13]] has a number. The notes in the code, called comments, use those numbers. Rules 12 to 14 are for logging in, and chapter 6 adds them.
Rules 1, 2 and 3: the username is not blank, has 3 to 12 characters, and uses only letters and numbers.
Rule 4: nobody else has the username. PlayerFile checks this one, because only PlayerFile reads the file.
Rules 5 and 6: the password is not blank, and has 6 to 20 characters.
Rules 7 and 8: the password has a letter and a number, and has no bar `|` in it.
Rules 9 and 10: the second password box is not blank, and matches the first one.
Rule 11: the player has clicked an avatar.
A bar `|` in a password would break `players.txt`, because the bar splits each line into its parts. That is why rule 8 is there.

screens.title: Add Exceptions.cs, and type the first 2 exceptions

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, your project has SummitException, and a BlankFieldException that inherits from it.
C# has its own Exception class. SummitException [[inherits|5]] from it, and every other exception in the game inherits from SummitException. So one `catch` for SummitException catches them all.

code.title: Exceptions.cs: SummitException
partLines: `: Exception` means SummitException inherits from C#'s own Exception class. The constructor is the part that sets up a new exception. It takes the message, and `: base(message)` hands it to Exception, which keeps it. The empty `{ }` means it needs no lines of its own.

code.title: BlankFieldException
partLines: BlankFieldException inherits from SummitException. It is thrown when a box is empty, with a message that names the box, such as **Type a username.**

stages.title: Add the rules to Player and PlayerFile

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, Username throws an exception if the username is blank, too short, too long or has a bad symbol.
The rules go in the `set` part, so a bad username is refused the moment code tries to set it. The new version of Username comes in a copy with a gap, and you type the rules into the gap.

code.title: Username, with rules 1, 2 and 3
code.why: The comment, get and set lines are the same shape as the Username you typed in chapter 3.
partLines: The comment now names the rules. `get` is the same as in chapter 3.
`Trim()` takes off any spaces at the start and the end. If nothing is left, the username is blank.
`||` means or: too short or too long. The exception is handed the length, and makes its own message.
The loop looks at each character in turn. `char.IsLetterOrDigit` is true for a letter or a digit. `!` means not, so a space or a `|` is caught.
The field is set only if every rule passed, because each `throw` stops the method first. The trimmed name is kept, without its spaces.

screens.title: Add rules 5 to 8 to Password, and rule 11 to Avatar

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, Password and Avatar throw an exception when one of their rules is broken.
Password has 4 rules. Rule 7 needs 2 `bool` values (a `bool` is either true or false). They start false and turn true when the loop finds a letter or a number.

code.title: Password, with rules 5, 6, 7 and 8
code.why: The comment, get, set and the last line are the same shape as the Password you typed in chapter 3.
partLines: The comment now names the rules. A password is never trimmed, because a space can be part of it.
The message is long, so it goes on a second line. C# reads both lines as one, up to the `;`.
`hasLetter` and `hasNumber` start false. The loop turns each one true when it finds a letter or a digit. If either is still false after the loop, the password needs a letter or a number.
`Contains` is true if the bar is anywhere in the password. The bar is in single quotes, because it is one `char`.
The field is set only if all 4 rules passed.

screens.title: Test every rule with the Test button

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you know that every rule throws the right message, and that a good player is still added.
Change one value in btnTest_Click, press F5, then click Test. A row marked **Must be refused** must show its message and not add the player.

check.how: The message must say **Type a username.**
check.fix: Check rule 1 in Username, and the `Trim()` on its first line.

check.what: Set the username to `fell walker`, with a space in it.
check.how: The message must say **Your username can only use letters and numbers. Take out the space.**
check.fix: Check rule 3 in Username. The `!` before `char.IsLetterOrDigit` must be there.

check.how: The message must say **The username testClimber is already taken. Try another one.**
check.fix: Check rule 4 in Add, and that `Exists` is called before the StreamWriter.

check.what: Set the username to `rulesTester`, and the password to `ropeclimb`.
check.how: The message must say **Your password needs at least one letter and one number.**
check.fix: Check rule 7 in Password: `hasNumber` turns true only in the `char.IsDigit` line.

check.what: Keep `rulesTester`, and set the password to `rope|26`.
check.how: The message must say **Your password cannot use the | character.**

check.what: Keep `rulesTester`, set the password back to `rope2026`, and set the avatar to `""`.
check.how: The message must say **Click a picture to choose your avatar.**

check.what: Keep `rulesTester` and `rope2026`, and set the avatar back to `avatar-fox.png`.
check.how: The message says **Added:** and shows the line for rulesTester. The player is at the end of `players.txt`.
check.fix: If a rule message shows instead, check that rule against its yellow lines.

code.title: Test rules 9 and 10
task: In btnTest_Click, set the username to one that is not taken yet.
Add the yellow line above `PlayerFile.Add(p);`, inside the try block.
Make the two passwords different and run the test. Then make the second password blank and run it again.
Then make the 2 passwords the same, and run it a third time.
code.test: Press F5 and click Test after each change.
code.expect: First: **The two passwords are different. Type them both again.** Then: **Type your password again.** Then: **Added:**, with the new player's line.
code.hint: CheckPasswordsMatch is `static`, which means you call it by its class name. Start the line with Player, not with `p`.

glossary: char.IsDigit
Says whether one letter of some text is a digit, from 0 to 9.
Contains
`value.Contains("|")` is true when the bar is anywhere in the text.
try and catch
Code inside `try` runs. If it throws an exception, the matching `catch` runs, and the program does not crash.
exception
A message the code sends out when something has gone wrong. It stops the code until a `catch` deals with it.
throw
`throw` stops the method at once, and hands an exception to whatever code called it.
inherit
A class that inherits from another class gets everything the other class has. `: SummitException` after a class name means it inherits from SummitException.
base
`: base(message)` hands the message to the class it inherits from, which keeps it.
try
A `try` block holds code that might throw an exception.
catch
A `catch` block runs when code in the `try` block throws an exception.
Message
The words an exception carries, such as **Type a username.**
Trim
Takes the spaces off the start and the end of some words.
Length
How many characters some words have.
char
One character, such as a letter, a digit or a space.
rule
Something a player must do, such as type a username of 3 to 12 characters. Each rule is checked in the code.
